title: Incremental status threads — customer-facing runbook and sample updates
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, customer-facing runbook for writing incremental status threads on the status page and email/partner notices during multi-wave inference degradations. Primary goal: produce short, repeatable messages that reduce customer confusion while engineering iterates on mitigation. Secondary goal: capture artifacts customers may request for reconciliation/replay.

Context (short):
- Incident class: partial-region increased tail latency caused by unexpected KV cache churn after a model rollout + autoscaler oscillation.
- Customer-visible symptoms: slower streaming responses (stuttered tokens), occasional truncated structured outputs, rate-limited retries on heavy routes.

Draft communication cadence (skeleton):
1) Acknowledged (T+0 to T+15): one-sentence summary + scope + immediate customer impact + statement that we have an active investigation.
   - sample: "We are aware of increased tail latency impacting streaming responses in EU and us-west regions for certain customers (affecting ~3% of requests). Engineers are investigating."
2) Investigating (T+15 to T+60): short update with suspected subsystem and next expected update time. Avoid deep technical jargon.
   - sample: "Initial signals indicate elevated KV cache eviction and autoscaler churn coincident with a model rollout. We are collecting traces and will provide a mitigation ETA within 30–45 minutes."
3) Mitigating (when a mitigation is in flight): indicate actions being taken and workarounds customers can apply.
   - sample: "Mitigation: rolling back the rollout and tuning autoscaler thresholds for affected pools. Customers can reduce risk by pinning model variants or enabling request-level fallback (see FAQ)."
4) Monitoring / Progress (post-mitigation): confirm observed improvements and continuing checks.
5) Resolved + Postmortem link (final): summary of root cause, impact window, customer-facing remediation, and replay/evidence package.

Customer FAQ (short answers for status page):
Q: Which customers were affected?
A: A subset of hosted API customers receiving inference from EU and us-west GPU pools during the rollout window. We will provide a list of impacted tenant IDs to partners upon request.

Q: Do I need to replay requests?
A: Most successful responses remain intact. If you observed truncated or inconsistent structured-output for high-priority customers, we can provide an evidence package and replay guidance (see linked artifacts).

Q: Can I avoid this in future?
A: Short-term: pin requests to stable model variants or enable model-fallback to lower-capacity variants. Long-term: we will propose config guardrails for rollout and autoscaler changes (in postmortem).

Evidence package contents (what ops will prepare for customers on request):
- per-tenant request IDs (time-window)
- sampling of request/response payloads (redacted)
- trace IDs and span timestamps
- autoscaler and cache eviction metrics for the impacted pools

Operational notes for the comms author (how to write incremental posts):
- Keep updates <= 3 short paragraphs on status page; subject line for email should be concise ("Redwood: Investigating increased inference latency in EU")
- Use plain language first sentence: what, who, and when
- If you must include technical detail, add a single line prefaced with "For technical customers: ..."
- Include links to the evidence request form and partner-replay instructions in every update after T+30
- Avoid promising exact ETAs; use ranges (e.g., "30–90 minutes")

Action items (todo):
- [ ] Finalize list of impacted tenant IDs with infra (owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Prepare evidence package template (owner: SRE oncall)
- [ ] Draft postmortem narrative and customer FAQ for final update (owner: Eleanor)
- [ ] Create rollback checklist for future rollouts (owner: platform-eng)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we offer automatic credits for affected customers or handle on a case-by-case basis? (ops/legal)
- Should we publish raw eviction and autoscaler metrics on the status page as a link for transparency? Pros/cons noted in thread.

Sample final postmortem blurb (customer-facing):
"Summary: On 2029-09-10 between 10:12–11:05 UTC Redwood observed increased tail latency in EU and us-west GPU pools caused by unexpected KV cache churn following a model rollout. The symptom impacted streaming token pacing for a subset of hosted API requests; no customer data loss was detected. We rolled back the rollout and adjusted autoscaler thresholds to stabilize cache residency."

Contact + escalation:
- Customer success triage: cs-triage@redwood.ai
- Partner & enterprise contacts: named account reps (we will attach a per-customer evidence package on request)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep status posts terse; customers get overwhelmed by long walls of text. Use bullets.
- Save final artifacts in ops-replay/2029-09-cache-churn for audit.

Revision history:
- 2029-09-10: initial draft (Eleanor)
- 2029-09-12: added FAQ + evidence package checklist (Marcus)
- 2029-09-15: clarified communication cadence and examples (Sofia)

(End of doc)
